The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6-derived CMT2 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts and chimeric mice were bred to C57BL/6 mice. The FRT-flanked neo cassette was removed in the germline mice by intercrossing with a Flpe-deleter strain on a mixed B6;SJL background (see Stock No. 003800). The resulting mutant offspring (now harboring this DATIREScre allele) were maintained on this mixed genetic background prior to arrival at The Jackson Laboratory. Upon arrival, mice were backcrossed to the C57BL/6J inbred strain (Stock No. 000664) for at least five generations. development: Exon 8 (NM_001077411.4) of the mouse Gba1 gene was modified using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies to incorporate an E344K (GAG->AAG) knock-in (bold) and 3 silent mutations (lower case): wildtype CCAAAGCTACTTTAGGAGAGACA to mutant CtAAgGCcACTTTAGGAAAGACA. SgRNA TGTCTCTCCTAAAGTAGCTT, donor DNA, and Cas9 mRNA were injected into hybrid embryos (MF1 outbred ; C57BL/6 inbred). The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 8 generations (see SNP note below). The donating laboratory sent 2 homozygous males (black coat color) to The Jackson Laboratory in 2022. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2022, a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (~9000 SNP) analysis was performed on the 2 males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. These data showed ~97-99% C57BL/6 markers (~89-92% C57BL/6J ; ~7-8% C57BL/6NCrl). The remaining 1-3% of the markers were of unknown origin, which may represent MF1 outbred contribution from the embryos used in creating the mice. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J. development: Exon 8 (NM_001077411.4) of the mouse Gba1 gene was modified using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies to incorporate an E344K (GAG->AAG) knock-in (bold) and 3 silent mutations (lower case): wildtype CCAAAGCTACTTTAGGAGAGACA to mutant CtAAgGCcACTTTAGGAAAGACA. SgRNA TGTCTCTCCTAAAGTAGCTT, donor DNA, and Cas9 mRNA were injected into hybrid embryos (MF1 outbred ; C57BL/6 inbred). The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 8 generations (see SNP note below). The donating laboratory sent 2 homozygous males (black coat color) to The Jackson Laboratory in 2022. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2022, a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (~9000 SNP) analysis was performed on the 2 males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. These data showed ~97-99% C57BL/6 markers (~89-92% C57BL/6J ; ~7-8% C57BL/6NCrl). The remaining 1-3% of the markers were of unknown origin, which may represent MF1 outbred contribution from the embryos used in creating the mice. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J. Browse References > Detailed Description In Parkinson's disease, dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the midbrain gradually degenerate, with ventral substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) DANs exhibiting greater vulnerability. Slc6a3 (solute carrier family 6 (neurotransmitter transporter, dopamine), member 3; also called DAT) encodes a dopamine transporter protein and is expressed in dopaminergic neurons. DAT-FlpO (also called DAT-Flp or Slc6a3-T2A-FlpO) mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Slc6a3 promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. When crossed with animals carrying FRT-flanked sequences, the FRT'ed region is excised in Slc6a3-expressing cells of the offspring. Characterization of the DAT-FlpO line expression and examination of whole-brain efferent and afferent connectivity of dopaminergic neuron subtypes was accomplished through crosses with an unspecified Ai65 Flp reporter line. TdTomato+ cells were confirmed to be tyrosine hydroxylase positive (TH+) neurons. (Fushiki, 2024; PMID 39763754) Read More Development The TAA stop codon in exon 15 of the mouse Slc6a3 gene (ENSMUST00000022100.6) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO-rBG (rabbit β-globin polyadenylation signal)-pA cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: CCAACAGCCAATGGCGCAGCTGG). Two silent mutations aa.613 L(CTG to TTA), aa.614 R(CGC to AGG) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed 100% of the markers consistent with C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description In Parkinson's disease, dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the midbrain gradually degenerate, with ventral substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) DANs exhibiting greater vulnerability. Slc6a3 (solute carrier family 6 (neurotransmitter transporter, dopamine), member 3; also called DAT) encodes a dopamine transporter protein and is expressed in dopaminergic neurons. DAT-FlpO (also called DAT-Flp or Slc6a3-T2A-FlpO) mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Slc6a3 promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. When crossed with animals carrying FRT-flanked sequences, the FRT'ed region is excised in Slc6a3-expressing cells of the offspring. Characterization of the DAT-FlpO line expression and examination of whole-brain efferent and afferent connectivity of dopaminergic neuron subtypes was accomplished through crosses with an unspecified Ai65 Flp reporter line. TdTomato+ cells were confirmed to be tyrosine hydroxylase positive (TH+) neurons. (Fushiki, 2024; PMID 39763754) Read More Development The TAA stop codon in exon 15 of the mouse Slc6a3 gene (ENSMUST00000022100.6) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO-rBG (rabbit β-globin polyadenylation signal)-pA cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: CCAACAGCCAATGGCGCAGCTGG). Two silent mutations aa.613 L(CTG to TTA), aa.614 R(CGC to AGG) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed 100% of the markers consistent with C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description A2a-Cre mice express Cre recombinase from the mouse Adora2a (adenosine A2a receptor) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Cre recombinase-dependent constructs to target Adora2a-expressing cells and the dopamine 2 (D2)/adenosine A2a receptor neuronal subpopulation that marks the indirect pathway of the striatum. They offer a fully characterized alternative to existing BAC transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), Dr-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 3 of the mouse Adora2a gene (ENSMUST00000105420) on mouse Chromosome 10 was replaced with a T2A-Cre cassette using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: AGGCTGTTCCTACCCTACCCTGG). Two synonymous mutations, p.A394 (GCC to GCA) and p.R397 (AGG to CGC), were also introduced to exon 3 to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for 4 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed at least 97.1% of the markers as C57BL/6J. Browse References > Detailed Description A2a-FlpO mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Adora2a (adenosine A2a receptor) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Flp recombinase-dependent constructs to target Adora2a-expressing cells and the dopamine 2 (D2)/adenosine A2a receptor neuronal subpopulation that marks the indirect pathway of the striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 3 of the mouse Adora2a gene (ENSMUST00000105420.2) on mouse Chromosome 10 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO cassette using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: AGGCTGTTCCTACCCTACCCTGG). Two silent mutations (aa. 394A (GCC to GCA) and aa. 397R (AGG to CGC)) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed at least 97.1% of the markers as C57BL/6J. Additionally, one region was identified having markers other than C57BL/6 present on Chromosome 10 ~48.6-75.6 Mb (likely reflecting the Adora2a-T2A-FlpO mutation at Chromosome 10 ~75 Mb). These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were on a C57BL/6J genetic background. description: Mutations in human GBA1 (glucosidase, beta, acid 1) can cause Gaucher disease, an autosomal recessive lysosomal (lipid) storage disease, and have been associated with late onset Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia. These mice express the mutant D427V Gba1 protein, which corresponds to the D409V mutation in the mature human GBA1 protein, and possess loxP sites flanking exons 6 through 8. Mice that are heterozygous for the targeted mutation are viable and fertile. Homozygous Gba1 D409V knock-in mice show a significant reduction in Gba1 protein level and glucocerebrosidase activity, and a significant increase in glucosylsphingosine in both brain and liver tissues. Heterozygotes demonstrate significant cognitive impairment by the age of 12 months, as determined by both Morris water maze and Y-maze behavioral tests (PMID: 31299418). When these mutant mice are bred to mice that express Cre recombinase, resulting offspring will have exons 6 through 8 deleted in the cre-expressing tissues and will no longer express the mutant D427V protein. Preliminary characterization was presented in a poster at the 2015 Society for Neuroscience conference. Read More

development: A targeting vector containing a FRT site flanked NEO cassette, and a F3 FRT site flanked PurO cassette was used to introduce the D427V point mutation into exon 10. The FRT site flanked NEO cassette was inserted into intron 5 and the F3 FRT site flanked PurO cassette was inserted into intron 8. In addition, loxP sites were inserted to flank exons 6 through 8. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6NTac derived Art B6 3.6 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into BALB/c blastocysts. The resulting chimeric animals were crossed to FLP recombinase expressing females on the C57BL/6NTac background, C57BL/6NTac-Tg(CAG-Flpe)2Art, to remove the selection cassettes (see SNP results below). These mice no longer carry the FLP recombinase allele. Upon arrival at The Jackson Laboratory, the mice were crossed to C57BL/6N (Stock No. 005304) at least once to establish the colony. A 32 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 27 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. While the 27 markers throughout the genome suggested a C57BL/6 genetic background, 4 of 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N were found to be segregating. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a mixed C57BL/6J ; C57BL/6N genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description D1-Cre mice express Cre recombinase from the mouse Drd1 (dopamine receptor 1) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Cre recombinase-dependent constructs to target Drd1-expressing cells and mark the direct pathway spiny projection neuronal subpopulation in striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. They offer a fully characterized alternative to existing BAC transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 2 of the mouse Drd1 gene (ENSMUT00000021932) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-Cre cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: GAGATGAGAACCCAATATTCAGG). Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 5 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). Browse References > Detailed Description D1-Cre mice express Cre recombinase from the mouse Drd1 (dopamine receptor 1) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Cre recombinase-dependent constructs to target Drd1-expressing cells and mark the direct pathway spiny projection neuronal subpopulation in striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. They offer a fully characterized alternative to existing BAC transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 2 of the mouse Drd1 gene (ENSMUT00000021932) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-Cre cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: GAGATGAGAACCCAATATTCAGG). Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 5 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). Browse References > Detailed Description α-Synuclein is a neuronal protein (coded by Snca) which plays a role in synaptic plasticity and neurotransmitter release. Mutations of Snca have been implicated in a group of neurodegenerative diseases that result from an accumulation of α-synuclein in neurons or, in some cases, glial cells. These disorders include Parkinson's disease (PDD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), the Lewy body variant of Alzheimer's disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation. These humanized A53T SNCA-GR (gene replacement) knock-in/knock-out mice carry a 158 kb fragment of human SNCA replacing the mouse Snca locus and the pathogenic A53T mutation (alanine to threonine) associated with early -onset Parkinson's disease. Mice homozygous for the mutation are viable and fertile with no obvious phenotype. These mice may be useful for studying SNCA function. Of note, the SNCA-GR model set also includes: B6J.B6N-Sncatm1.1(SNCA)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039166) and B6J.B6N-Sncatm3.1(SNCA*E46K)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039168). Read More Development The A53T SNCA-GR targeting vector was designed to insert a 158 kb (Chr4:89,707,185-89,865,027) fragment of the human SNCA (synuclein, alpha) carrying the A53T (alanine to threonine) mutation in place of Chr6:60,683,985-60,848,702 of the mouse Snca gene on chromosome 6. The genomic sequences are from human assembly GRCh38.p14 and the mouse assembly GRCm39. The construct included a loxP-flanked neomycin selection cassette. In addition, there is also a SNCA non-coding antisense RNA in the human genome segment. The insertion disrupts Snca transcription. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6N-PRX-B6N embryonic stem cells (ES). The neomycin cassette was removed by transient expression of Cre. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts. The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J mice for at least 5 generations (see SNP note below) prior to sending males to The Jackson Laboratory Repository in 2024. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2024, a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (~9000 SNP) analysis was performed on the 2 males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. These data support a C57BL/6 genetic background predominantly comprised of C57BL/6J. The existence of the human genomic sequences may contribute to inability of data interpretation to predict percentages. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J allele-type with the exception of one marker (Chr.8 ~58 Mb) being heterozygous for C57BL/6J;C57BL/6N allele-type. Taken together, this suggests the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were predominantly C57BL/6J with some remaining contributions from C57BL/6N. Browse References > Detailed Description α-Synuclein is a neuronal protein (coded by Snca) which plays a role in synaptic plasticity and neurotransmitter release. Mutations of Snca have been implicated in a group of neurodegenerative diseases that result from an accumulation of α-synuclein in neurons or, in some cases, glial cells. These disorders include Parkinson's disease (PDD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), the Lewy body variant of Alzheimer's disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation. These humanized A53T SNCA-GR (gene replacement) knock-in/knock-out mice carry a 158 kb fragment of human SNCA replacing the mouse Snca locus and the pathogenic A53T mutation (alanine to threonine) associated with early -onset Parkinson's disease. Mice homozygous for the mutation are viable and fertile with no obvious phenotype. These mice may be useful for studying SNCA function. Of note, the SNCA-GR model set also includes: B6J.B6N-Sncatm1.1(SNCA)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039166) and B6J.B6N-Sncatm3.1(SNCA*E46K)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039168). Read More Development The A53T SNCA-GR targeting vector was designed to insert a 158 kb (Chr4:89,707,185-89,865,027) fragment of the human SNCA (synuclein, alpha) carrying the A53T (alanine to threonine) mutation in place of Chr6:60,683,985-60,848,702 of the mouse Snca gene on chromosome 6. The genomic sequences are from human assembly GRCh38.p14 and the mouse assembly GRCm39. The construct included a loxP-flanked neomycin selection cassette. In addition, there is also a SNCA non-coding antisense RNA in the human genome segment. The insertion disrupts Snca transcription. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6N-PRX-B6N embryonic stem cells (ES). The neomycin cassette was removed by transient expression of Cre. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts. The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J mice for at least 5 generations (see SNP note below) prior to sending males to The Jackson Laboratory Repository in 2024. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2024, a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (~9000 SNP) analysis was performed on the 2 males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. These data support a C57BL/6 genetic background predominantly comprised of C57BL/6J. The existence of the human genomic sequences may contribute to inability of data interpretation to predict percentages. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J allele-type with the exception of one marker (Chr.8 ~58 Mb) being heterozygous for C57BL/6J;C57BL/6N allele-type. Taken together, this suggests the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were predominantly C57BL/6J with some remaining contributions from C57BL/6N. development: The Rab32*S69Rflox knock-in allele was designed to incorporate the S69R (AGC to AGG) mutation in exon 1 of the RAB32, member RAS oncogene family (Rab32) gene. The targeting construct consists of an initial loxP site, an F3-flanked puromycin cassette, mutant exon 1 harboring the S69R mutation, an FRT-flanked neomycin cassette, and second loxP site. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6J-derived ICS embryonic stem (ES) cells and correctly targeted ES cells were injected into recipient blastocysts. Chimeric mice were crossed to C57BL/6J mice to confirm germline transmission. The resulting Rab32*S69Rflox mice were crossed to a FLP recombinase mouse line, on a C57BL/6 background (OzFlp), to remove the F3 and FRT-flanked puromycin/neomycin cassettes. Rab32*S69Rflox mice were then backcrossed to C57BL/6J for at least 1 generation by the donating laboratory prior to sending males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J (Stock No. 000664) oocytes. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed more than 99.4% of the markers as C57BL/6J. Browse References > Detailed Description Point mutations and duplications in the SNCA (synuclein, alpha) gene cause familial forms of Parkinson’s disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). The gene regulates vesicle exocytosis, but in the disease state forms insoluble deposits that cause extensive cytopathology and neuronal loss. 3K (3K-3817) mice carry the human familial Parkinson's disease associated E46K mutation in addition to two homologous E-to-K mutations into the adjacent KTKEGV repeats (E35K and E61K). The transgene is expressed pan-neuronally from the mouse Thy1 (thymus cell antigen 1, theta) promoter in the brain. This results in a loss of tetramers and gain of monomers in transgenic mouse brain. These monomers are post-translationally modified, e.g. phospho-serine 129, and aggregate similar to PD. Excess monomers cluster in the nigral and cortical neurons and induce fiber and neuronal loss. The PD-type motor phenotypes are partly responsive to induces L-DOPA. Hemizygotes begin demonstrating a robust Parkinson's disease phenotypes starting at 2-3 months of age, including body tremor and gait abnormalities. Limb rigidity is more severe in males. For best breeding results, crosses of hemizygous females aged 3‐6 months with non-carrier or C57BL/6J (Stock No. 000664) males is recommended. Limb clasping hinders breeding abilities in male 3K mice that are older than 3 months of age. Large-sized pan-neuronal phosphorylated-serine 129 (pS129) inclusions that are proteinase K resistant increase between 3-6 months of age (PMIDs: 30308173, 32996158, 35445353). Control strain WT-3877 (Stock No. 041613) expression levels match those of the 3K mutant line and are approximately 2-3 fold higher than endogenous mouse SNCA levels. The Jackson Laboratory also maintains stocks of the 3KL founder line 3798 (3KL-3798; Stock No. 032799) which has "low overexpression" of human SNCA similar that of endogenous mouse SNCA. Homozygotes of the 3KL line exhibit subtle motor impairment at 8 to 10 months of age. Read More Development Site-directed mutagenesis of full-length human wild-type α-synuclein (SNCA) cDNA was used to introduce the E35K, E46K, and E61K mutations (GAG to AAG). The modified human SNCA cDNA was used as the source for the Thy1-3K αS transgene, in which the mutant human SNCA is under control of the Thy1.2 (Thy1, thymus cell antigen 1, theta) neuronal regulator promoter. The transgene was microinjected into the pronucleus of C57BL/6J one-cell embryos. Founder line 3817 was subsequently established. The integration site and copy number of the transgene are unknown, but protein expression levels are ~2-3 times the endogenous mouse SNCA levels. The 3K (3K-3817) transgenic mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6NCrl for 4-5 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). Browse References > Detailed Description Point mutations and duplications in the SNCA (synuclein, alpha) gene cause familial forms of Parkinson’s disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). The gene regulates vesicle exocytosis, but in the disease state forms insoluble deposits that cause extensive cytopathology and neuronal loss. 3K (3K-3817) mice carry the human familial Parkinson's disease associated E46K mutation in addition to two homologous E-to-K mutations into the adjacent KTKEGV repeats (E35K and E61K). The transgene is expressed pan-neuronally from the mouse Thy1 (thymus cell antigen 1, theta) promoter in the brain. This results in a loss of tetramers and gain of monomers in transgenic mouse brain. These monomers are post-translationally modified, e.g. phospho-serine 129, and aggregate similar to PD. Excess monomers cluster in the nigral and cortical neurons and induce fiber and neuronal loss. The PD-type motor phenotypes are partly responsive to induces L-DOPA. Hemizygotes begin demonstrating a robust Parkinson's disease phenotypes starting at 2-3 months of age, including body tremor and gait abnormalities. Limb rigidity is more severe in males. For best breeding results, crosses of hemizygous females aged 3‐6 months with non-carrier or C57BL/6J (Stock No. 000664) males is recommended. Limb clasping hinders breeding abilities in male 3K mice that are older than 3 months of age. Large-sized pan-neuronal phosphorylated-serine 129 (pS129) inclusions that are proteinase K resistant increase between 3-6 months of age (PMIDs: 30308173, 32996158, 35445353). Control strain WT-3877 (Stock No. 041613) expression levels match those of the 3K mutant line and are approximately 2-3 fold higher than endogenous mouse SNCA levels. The Jackson Laboratory also maintains stocks of the 3KL founder line 3798 (3KL-3798; Stock No. 032799) which has "low overexpression" of human SNCA similar that of endogenous mouse SNCA. Homozygotes of the 3KL line exhibit subtle motor impairment at 8 to 10 months of age. Read More Development Site-directed mutagenesis of full-length human wild-type α-synuclein (SNCA) cDNA was used to introduce the E35K, E46K, and E61K mutations (GAG to AAG). The modified human SNCA cDNA was used as the source for the Thy1-3K αS transgene, in which the mutant human SNCA is under control of the Thy1.2 (Thy1, thymus cell antigen 1, theta) neuronal regulator promoter. The transgene was microinjected into the pronucleus of C57BL/6J one-cell embryos. Founder line 3817 was subsequently established. The integration site and copy number of the transgene are unknown, but protein expression levels are ~2-3 times the endogenous mouse SNCA levels. The 3K (3K-3817) transgenic mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6NCrl for 4-5 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). No gene product (mRNA) is detected by RT-PCR analysis of embryonic fibroblasts and kidney. Immunohistochemical analysis of kidney and bone tissue also fails to detect gene product (protein). Homozygotes exhibit disorganized ultrastructural wound matrix remodeling and defective macrophage infiltration and accumulation at sites of injury and infection. Experimentally induced hyperoxaluria results in renal tubule deposition of calcium oxalate crystals. Accelerated ectopic calcification mineralization in soft tissues occurs after subcutaneous implantation of glutaraldehyde-fixed aortic valve tissue. Mutant macrophage response to mycobacteria infection and pulmonary granulomatous response and inflammation are impaired. According to a recent publication (Hsieh et al 2006 Cancer Res 2006 66:7119-27), mutant mice treated with a skin chemical carcinogenesis protocol show a marked decrease both in tumor/papilloma incidence and multiplicity compared with wildtype. This mutant mouse strain may be useful in studies of tissue remodeling, wound repair, fibrosis and granulomatous diseases. phenotype: . Prior to Cre-mediated recombination, homozygous LRRK2 flox-R1441G mice demonstrate LRRK2 protein levels in brain tissue similar to wildtype controls. development: The LRRK2 flox-R1441G knock-in allele was designed to incorporate a conditional R1441G point mutation into exon 31 of the leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (Lrrk2) gene based on the NCBI transcript NM_025730.3 (Ensembl transcript ENSMUST00000060642). The targeting vector, which was inserted into the endogenous Lrrk2 intron 30, consists of an initial loxP site, followed by an FRT-flanked neomycin cassette, exons 31-51 Lrrk2 cDNA including the 3' untranslated region (UTR), an hGHpA (2.1 kb of the human growth hormone gene harboring the hGH polyadenylation signal), an F3-flanked puromycin cassette, and a second loxP site. Genomic exon 31 harboring the R1441G mutation is located immediately downstream of the second loxP site. The target construct was electroporated into C57BL/6N-derived embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into recipient blastocysts. The resulting chimeric mice were bred to FLP-recombinase mice, on a C57BL/6N background, to remove the FRT-flanked neomycin cassette and the F3-flanked puromycin cassette. The donating laboratory reported they maintained this mouse line on a C57BL/6N background prior to sending homozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6NJ (Stock No. 005304) oocytes. In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the homozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6N allele-type. In 2025, the homozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed 98.6-100% of the markers as C57BL/6. The scoring algorithm was unable to discern the C57BL/6 substrain with any certainty. Additionally, one mouse was identified potentially having markers other than C57BL/6 present on Chromosome 19 ~45.45-46.8 Mb (this was not examined further). These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were on a C57BL/6 genetic background. These LRRK2 flox-R1441G mice possess loxP sites flanking wildtype exons 31-51 of the Lrrk2 gene and a mutant exon 31, carrying the R1441G missense mutation, inserted immediately downstream of the second loxP site. Homozygous mice are viable and fertile with no overt phenotype. Prior to Cre-mediated recombination, homozygous LRRK2 flox-R1441G mice demonstrate LRRK2 protein levels in brain tissue similar to wildtype controls. After Cre-mediated recombination, the wildtype exons 31-51 will be excised and the mutant exon 31 with the R1441G mutation is expressed in cre-expressing tissues. These mice may be useful for studying hereditary Parkinson's disease. Read More Development The LRRK2 flox-R1441G knock-in allele was designed to incorporate a conditional R1441G point mutation into exon 31 of the leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (Lrrk2) gene based on the NCBI transcript NM_025730.3 (Ensembl transcript ENSMUST00000060642). The targeting vector, which was inserted into the endogenous Lrrk2 intron 30, consists of an initial loxP site, followed by an FRT-flanked neomycin cassette, exons 31-51 Lrrk2 cDNA including the 3' untranslated region (UTR), an hGHpA (2.1 kb of the human growth hormone gene harboring the hGH polyadenylation signal), an F3-flanked puromycin cassette, and a second loxP site. Genomic exon 31 harboring the R1441G mutation is located immediately downstream of the second loxP site. The target construct was electroporated into C57BL/6N-derived embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into recipient blastocysts. The resulting chimeric mice were bred to FLP-recombinase mice, on a C57BL/6N background, to remove the FRT-flanked neomycin cassette and the F3-flanked puromycin cassette. The donating laboratory reported they maintained this mouse line on a C57BL/6N background prior to sending homozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6NJ (Stock No. 005304) oocytes. In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the homozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6N allele-type. In 2025, the homozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed 98.6-100% of the markers as C57BL/6. The scoring algorithm was unable to discern the C57BL/6 substrain with any certainty. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were on a C57BL/6 genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description Ercc1- mice carry a targeted knock-out of the mouse Ercc1 (excision repair cross-complementing rodent repair deficiency, complementation group 1) gene. A neomycin cassette was introduced to the last coding exon (exon 7), preventing the essential expression of 74 essential carboxy terminal amino acids. Expression analysis shows an absence of transcript in mouse embryonic fibroblasts derived from homozygous mutant mice. Ercc1- homozygotes demonstrate retarded growth, enlarged liver nuclei, and greatly reduced lifespan (3-8 weeks). Homozygotes are born in reduced numbers (many dying by embryonic day 13.5) when bred on a pure C57BL/6 or FVB background. Therefore, experimental animals were only bred on a C57BL/6-FVB F1 genetic background by the donating laboratory. They exhibit an absence of subcutaneous fat, early onset of ferritin deposition in the spleen, kidney malfunction, gross abnormalities of ploidy, and cytoplasmic invaginations in nuclei of liver and kidney, and compromised nucleotide excision repair (NER) and cross-link repair. In addition, ERCC1-mutant cells undergo premature replicative senescence. Heterozygotes are not known to exhibit any phenotype. (Weeda, 1997; PMID 9197240) This mutation is also available on a predominantly FVB genetic background (see Stock No. 040163), with homozygous animals reportedly surviving up to 10 weeks of age. The donating laboratory wishes to note that all of their compound mutant experiments (PMID 27556946, PMID 36756698, PMID 38498063, PMID 22953029, PMID 38689513, PMID 38451018) were performed on an F1 hybrid genetic background. This hybrid background was derived from crosses of C57BL/6JOlaHsd-background mutant animals with FVB/NHanHsd-background mutant animals (e.g. Ercc1+/- C57BL/6 x Ercc1d/+ FVB (Stock No. 040165)). The contributing single mutant alleles were maintained independently through crosses of heterozygotes with C57BL/6JOlaHsd or FVB/NHanHsd inbred mice rather than wildtype animals from within their colonies (e.g. Ercc1-/+ C57BL/6 x WT (Ercc1+/+) C57BL/6). They did not maintain homozygous colonies and their F1 mice were not further intercrossed. Read More Development A neomycin selection cassette, blocking the expression of 74 carboxy terminal amino acids, was introduced to exon 7 of the mouse Ercc1 gene via homologous recombination in 129P2/OlaHsd-derived E14 embryonic stem (ES) cells. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6JOlaHsd for more than 75 generations prior to sending heterozygous (Ercc1-) females and wildtype C57BL/6JOlaHsd males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, those females and males were used to rederive the colony. Subsequently, embryos will be cryopreserved. In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the heterozygous females and wildtype males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type as previously observed for other B6JOlaHsd mouse lines. In 2025, heterozygous females and wildtype males were sent to The Jackson Laboratory. Ercc1- mice carry a targeted knock-out of the mouse Ercc1 (excision repair cross-complementing rodent repair deficiency, complementation group 1) gene. A neomycin cassette was introduced to the last coding exon (exon 7), preventing the essential expression of 74 essential carboxy terminal amino acids. Expression analysis shows an absence of transcript in mouse embryonic fibroblasts derived from homozygous mutant mice.

Ercc1- homozygotes demonstrate retarded growth, enlarged liver nuclei, and greatly reduced lifespan (3-8 weeks). Homozygotes are born in reduced numbers (many dying by embryonic day 13.5) when bred on a pure C57BL/6 or FVB background. Therefore, experimental animals were only bred on a C57BL/6-FVB F1 genetic background by the donating laboratory. They exhibit an absence of subcutaneous fat, early onset of ferritin deposition in the spleen, kidney malfunction, gross abnormalities of ploidy, and cytoplasmic invaginations in nuclei of liver and kidney, and compromised nucleotide excision repair (NER) and cross-link repair. In addition, ERCC1-mutant cells undergo premature replicative senescence. Heterozygotes are not known to exhibit any phenotype. (Weeda, 1997; PMID 9197240)

This mutation is also available on a predominantly FVB genetic background (see Stock No. 040163), with homozygous animals reportedly surviving up to 10 weeks of age.

The donating laboratory wishes to note that all of their compound mutant experiments (PMID 27556946, PMID 36756698, PMID 38498063, PMID 22953029, PMID 38689513, PMID 38451018) were performed on an F1 hybrid genetic background. This hybrid background was derived from crosses of C57BL/6JOlaHsd-background mutant animals with FVB/NHanHsd-background mutant animals (e.g. Ercc1+/- C57BL/6 x Ercc1d/+ FVB (Stock No. 040165)). The contributing single mutant alleles were maintained independently through crosses of heterozygotes with C57BL/6JOlaHsd or FVB/NHanHsd inbred mice rather than wildtype animals from within their colonies (e.g. Ercc1-/+ C57BL/6 x WT (Ercc1+/+) C57BL/6). They did not maintain homozygous colonies and their F1 mice were not further intercrossed.

How it's Made Strain Highlights Congenic Transgenic Donating Investigator(s) Ted Dawson - Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Originating Article When using the TH-Cre 1 , TH-1 Cre mouse strain in a publication, please cite the originating article(s) and include JAX stock #008601 in your Materials and Methods section. Browse References > Detailed Description These transgenic mice express Cre recombinase under the control of the rat tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) promoter. The transgene integrated into chromosome 9 causing a 624 kbp deletion in 7630403G23Rik locus. Mice hemizygous for the TH-Cre transgene are viable and fertile, with the rat tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) promoter directing expression of Cre recombinase to catecholaminergic cells. Using crosses to reporter strains, cre activity is confirmed in catecholaminergic cells and is present in many of the projection areas of these neuronal populations. A mosaic of cre activity is noted in TH-positive neurons. Several other areas that are not typically thought to have active TH expression, including the lateral septal nucleus, accessory olfactory bulb, suparafascicular thalamus, and pretectal area, also exhibit Cre recombinase activity (possibly as a result of TH promoter activity in precursor cell populations or ectopic expression from the exogenous TH promoter). Some TH-negative cells closely clustered around and within TH-positive nuclei demonstrate cre activity. When bred with mice containing a loxP-flanked sequence of interest, Cre-mediated recombination will result in deletion of the floxed sequence(s) in the offspring. These TH-Cre transgenic mice are a tool for generating conditional mutations in catecholaminergic cells and may be useful for studying dopaminergic cell function, Parkinson's disease, and other neurodegenerative disorders. If the recombinase activity pattern of this allele is further characterized by the Genetic Resource Science group at The Jackson Laboratory, such findings will be reported on the Mouse Genome Informatics (MGI) Allele Detail entry (7630403G23RikTg(Th-cre)1Tmd). This same information would also be found searching the MGI Recombinase Activity database. The phenotype of homozygous mice has not been characterized, so appropriate caution should be taken with their use. mouse_summary: Background: (see SNP note below). In 2010 and 2011, a 32 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 27 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony (generation N6+F2, N6+F4 and N6+F6) at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. While the 27 markers throughout the genome suggested a C57BL/6 genetic background, all 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N were found to be segregating (each mouse having at least 1 marker segregating). These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository in 2009 were on a C57BL/6J or mixed C57BL/6J;C57BL/6N genetic background. In 2014, a cohort of mice from generation N6+F14 had 4 of the 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N fixed to C57BL/6N allele-type, with a single marker on chromosome 13 (~41.0 Mbp) fixed to C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2026, expanded quality control screening at The Jackson Laboratory tested more than 50 mice from Stock No. 008601. This showed all TH-Cre transgene carriers (n=94) genotyped positive for a kanamycin resistance sequence (kan), while all of their wildtype littermates (n=97) genotyped as negative for kan. This strongly suggests the TH-Cre transgene contains (or is closely linked to) a kan cassette. Browse References > Detailed Description These transgenic mice express Cre recombinase under the control of the rat tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) promoter. The transgene integrated into chromosome 9 causing a 624 kbp deletion in 7630403G23Rik locus. Mice hemizygous for the TH-Cre transgene are viable and fertile, with the rat tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) promoter directing expression of Cre recombinase to catecholaminergic cells. Using crosses to reporter strains, cre activity is confirmed in catecholaminergic cells and is present in many of the projection areas of these neuronal populations. A mosaic of cre activity is noted in TH-positive neurons. Some TH-negative cells closely clustered around and within TH-positive nuclei demonstrate cre activity. When bred with mice containing a loxP-flanked sequence of interest, Cre-mediated recombination will result in deletion of the floxed sequence(s) in the offspring. These TH-Cre transgenic mice are a tool for generating conditional mutations in catecholaminergic cells and may be useful for studying dopaminergic cell function, Parkinson's disease, and other neurodegenerative disorders. If the recombinase activity pattern of this allele is further characterized by the Genetic Resource Science group at The Jackson Laboratory, such findings will be reported on the Mouse Genome Informatics (MGI) Allele Detail entry (7630403G23RikTg(Th-cre)1Tmd). This same information would also be found searching the MGI Recombinase Activity database. The phenotype of homozygous mice has not been characterized, so appropriate caution should be taken with their use. While the 27 markers throughout the genome suggested a C57BL/6 genetic background, all 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N were found to be segregating (each mouse having at least 1 marker segregating). These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository in 2009 were on a C57BL/6J or mixed C57BL/6J;C57BL/6N genetic background. In 2014, a cohort of mice from generation N6+F14 had 4 of the 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N fixed to C57BL/6N allele-type, with a single marker on chromosome 13 (~41.0 Mbp) fixed to C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2026, expanded quality control screening at The Jackson Laboratory tested more than 50 mice from Stock No. 008601. This showed all TH-Cre transgene carriers (n=94) genotyped positive for a kanamycin resistance sequence (kan), while all of their wildtype littermates (n=97) genotyped as negative for kan. This strongly suggests the TH-Cre transgene contains (or is closely linked to) a kan cassette. Hemizygous Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) transgenic female mice are viable and fertile; hemizygous male mice are viable but demonstrate more severe deficits in cognition and motor function. The donating laboratory has determined that the Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) transgene integrated into the X chromosome and suggest maintaining a colony by breeding hemizygous Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) females with non-carrier (wildtype) males. Homozygous females have not been evaluated to date (September 2023). The donating investigator noted that these Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) transgenic mice demonstrate motor deficits, as measured by wire-hang test, as early as 1 month of age and become progressively more severe as the mice age compared to age-matched controls. These mice may be used when studying human neuronal α-synucleinopathies, such as Parkinson's disease. Distribution of this strain (Stock No. 038796) was supported by the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research. Read More Development The Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) transgene was generated using human synuclein, alpha (SNCA) cDNA under the control of the mouse Thy1 gene promoter. The wildtype human α-synuclein cDNA fragment (nt 53-475; Genbank accession No. L08850) was generated by RT-PCR from human brain mRNA, ligated into pCRII (Invitrogen, La Jolla, CA), sequenced for accuracy, and inserted into the mThy-1 expression cassette between exons 2 and 4. The purified linearized DNA was microinjected into the pronuclei of fertilized (C57BL/6 x DBA/2)F1 mouse oocytes. Founder line 61 was determined to have the highest expression and further expanded. The donating laboratory has indicated that the transgene integration site is on chromosome X; however, the copy number is not known. These transgenic mice were maintained on a mixed B6;D2 background. Upon arrival in December 2023, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize B6D2F1 (Stock No. 100006) oocytes. In 2023, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the males sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository. This confirmed the mixed C57BL/6;DBA/2 genetic background, with the C57BL/6 contributions being from C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N. Mutations of Snca have been implicated in a group of neurodegenerative diseases that result from an accumulation of α-synuclein in neurons or, in some cases, glial cells. These disorders include Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, the Lewy body variant of Alzheimer's disease (AD), multiple system atrophy, and neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation. Hemizygous Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) transgenic female mice are viable and fertile; hemizygous male mice are viable but demonstrate more severe deficits in cognition and motor function. The donating laboratory has determined that the Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) transgene integrated into the X chromosome and suggest maintaining a colony by breeding hemizygous Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) females with non-carrier (wildtype) males. Homozygous females have not been evaluated to date (September 2023). The donating investigator noted that these Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) transgenic mice demonstrate motor deficits, as measured by wire-hang test, as early as 1 month of age and become progressively more severe as the mice age compared to age-matched controls. These mice may be used when studying human neuronal α-synucleinopathies, such as Parkinson's disease. Distribution of this strain (Stock No. 038796) was supported by the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research. Read More Development The Line 61 (mThy-1 hα-synuclein) transgene was generated using human synuclein, alpha (SNCA) cDNA under the control of the mouse Thy1 gene promoter. The wildtype human α-synuclein cDNA fragment (nt 53-475; Genbank accession No. L08850) was generated by RT-PCR from human brain mRNA, ligated into pCRII (Invitrogen, La Jolla, CA), sequenced for accuracy, and inserted into the mThy-1 expression cassette between exons 2 and 4. The purified linearized DNA was microinjected into the pronuclei of fertilized (C57BL/6 x DBA/2)F1 mouse oocytes. Founder line 61 was determined to have the highest expression and further expanded. The donating laboratory has indicated that the transgene integration site is on chromosome X; however, the copy number is not known. These transgenic mice were maintained on a mixed B6;D2 background. Upon arrival in December 2023, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize B6D2F1 (Stock No. 100006) oocytes. In 2023, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the males sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository. This confirmed the mixed C57BL/6;DBA/2 genetic background, with the C57BL/6 contributions being from C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N. Browse References > Detailed Description α-Synuclein is a neuronal protein (coded by Snca) which plays a role in synaptic plasticity and neurotransmitter release. Mutations of Snca have been implicated in a group of neurodegenerative diseases that result from an accumulation of α-synuclein in neurons or, in some cases, glial cells. These disorders include Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, the Lewy body variant of Alzheimer's disease (AD), multiple system atrophy, and neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation. SNCA*E57K(16) transgenic mice express human α-synuclein that contains an E57K amino acid substitution driven by the mouse thymus cell antigen 1, theta (Thy1) promoter. This mutation results in expression of an altered α-synuclein that preferentially form oligomers, as opposed to fibrils. This oligomer-prone species of α-synuclein has been found to increase degeneration of dopaminergic neurons and synaptic damage. Hemizygous SNCA*E57K(16) transgenic mice are viable and fertile; homozygous SNCA*E57K(16) mice have not been evaluated by the donating laboratory (September 2023). The donating laboratory noted that these SNCA*E57K(16) transgenic mice displayed similar levels of synaptic degeneration and neuronal loss in the hippocampus when compared to transgenic mice harboring the full-length wildtype human α-synuclein (Stock No. 038796); however, they differed in that the oligomer-prone mice displayed more severe synaptic pathology, behavioral differences and neuronal loss in the frontal cortex. These mice may be used when studying human neuronal α-synucleinopathies, such as Parkinson's disease. Read More Development The SNCA*E57K(16) transgene was generated using human synuclein, alpha (SNCA) cDNA (GenBank# NM_000345), containing the E57K mutation, under the control of the mouse Thy1 gene promoter. The SNCA E57K cDNA fragment was ligated into pCRII (Invitrogen), sequenced for accuracy, inserted into the mThy-1 expression cassette between exons 2 and 4, and purified. The purified linearized DNA was microinjected into the pronuclei of fertilized (C57BL/6 x DBA/2)F1 mouse oocytes. Three founder lines were established, founder line 16 was determined to have the highest expression. The donating laboratory has indicated that the integration site and copy number are not known. These transgenic mice were then maintained on a mixed B6;D2 background. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize B6D2F1 (Stock No. 100006) oocytes. Browse References > Detailed Description α-Synuclein is a neuronal protein (coded by Snca) which plays a role in synaptic plasticity and neurotransmitter release. Mutations of Snca have been implicated in a group of neurodegenerative diseases that result from an accumulation of α-synuclein in neurons or, in some cases, glial cells. These disorders include Parkinson's disease (PDD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), the Lewy body variant of Alzheimer's disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation. These humanized wildtype SNCA-GR (gene replacement) knock-in/knock-out mice carry a 158 kb fragment of human SNCA replacing the mouse Snca locus. Mice homozygous for the mutation are viable and fertile with no obvious phenotype. These mice may be useful for studying SNCA function. Of note, the SNCA-GR model set also includes: B6J.B6N-Sncatm2.1(SNCA*A53T)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039167) and B6J.B6N-Sncatm3.1(SNCA*E46K)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039168). Read More Development The wildtype SNCA-GR targeting vector was designed to insert a 158 kb (Chr4:89,707,185-89,865,027) fragment of the human SNCA (synuclein, alpha) in place of Chr6:60,683,985-60,848,702 of the mouse Snca gene on chromosome 6. The genomic sequences are from human assembly GRCh38.p14 and the mouse assembly GRCm39. The construct included a loxP-flanked neomycin selection cassette. In addition, there is also a SNCA non-coding antisense RNA in the human genome segment. The insertion disrupts Snca transcription. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6N-PRX-B6N embryonic stem cells (ES). The neomycin cassette was removed by transient expression of Cre. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts. The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J mice for at least 5 generations (see SNP note below) prior to sending males to The Jackson Laboratory Repository in 2024. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2024, a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (~9000 SNP) analysis was performed on the 2 males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. These data support a C57BL/6 genetic background predominantly comprised of C57BL/6J. The existence of the human genomic sequences may contribute to inability of data interpretation to predict percentages. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J allele-type. Browse References > Detailed Description Ercc1- mice carry a targeted knock-out of the mouse Ercc1 (excision repair cross-complementing rodent repair deficiency, complementation group 1) gene. A neomycin cassette was introduced to the last coding exon (exon 7), preventing the expression of 74 essential carboxy terminal amino acids. Expression analysis shows an absence of transcript in mouse embryonic fibroblasts derived from homozygous mutant mice. Ercc1- homozygotes demonstrate retarded growth, enlarged liver nuclei, and greatly reduced lifespan (3-8 weeks). Homozygotes are born in reduced numbers (many dying by embryonic day 13.5) when bred on a pure C57BL/6 or FVB background. Therefore, experimental animals were only bred on a C57BL/6-FVB F1 genetic background by the donating laboratory. They exhibit an absence of subcutaneous fat, early onset of ferritin deposition in the spleen, kidney malfunction, gross abnormalities of ploidy, and cytoplasmic invaginations in nuclei of liver and kidney, and compromised nucleotide excision repair (NER) and cross-link repair. In addition, ERCC1-mutant cells undergo premature replicative senescence. Heterozygotes are not known to exhibit any phenotype. (Weeda, 1997; PMID 9197240) This mutation is also available on a predominantly C57BL/6-backcrossed genetic background (see Stock No. 040162), with homozygous animals reportedly surviving up to 38 days. The donating laboratory wishes to note that all of their compound mutant experiments (PMID 27556946, PMID 36756698, PMID 38498063, PMID 22953029, PMID 38689513, PMID 38451018) were performed on an F1 hybrid genetic background. This hybrid background was derived from crosses of C57BL/6JOlaHsd-background mutant animals with FVB/NHanHsd-background mutant animals (e.g. Ercc1+/- FVB x Ercc1d/+C57BL/6 (Stock No. 040165)). The contributing single mutant alleles were maintained independently through crosses of heterozygotes with C57BL/6JOlaHsd or FVB/NHanHsd inbred mice rather than wildtype animals from within their colonies (e.g. Ercc1-/+ FVB x WT (Ercc1+/+) FVB). They did not maintain homozygous colonies and their F1 mice were not further intercrossed. Resultant mice were backcrossed to FVB/NHanHsd for more than 75 generations by the donating laboratory prior to sending Ercc1- females and males to The Jackson Laboratory. Upon arrival, those females and males were used to rederive the colony. Subsequently, embryos will be cryopreserved. Ercc1- mice carry a targeted knock-out of the mouse Ercc1 (excision repair cross-complementing rodent repair deficiency, complementation group 1) gene. A neomycin cassette was introduced to the last coding exon (exon 7), preventing the expression of 74 essential carboxy terminal amino acids. Expression analysis shows an absence of transcript in mouse embryonic fibroblasts derived from homozygous mutant mice.

Ercc1- homozygotes demonstrate retarded growth, enlarged liver nuclei, and greatly reduced lifespan (3-8 weeks). Homozygotes are born in reduced numbers (many dying by embryonic day 13.5) when bred on a pure C57BL/6 or FVB background. Therefore, experimental animals were only bred on a C57BL/6-FVB F1 genetic background by the donating laboratory. They exhibit an absence of subcutaneous fat, early onset of ferritin deposition in the spleen, kidney malfunction, gross abnormalities of ploidy, and cytoplasmic invaginations in nuclei of liver and kidney, and compromised nucleotide excision repair (NER) and cross-link repair. In addition, ERCC1-mutant cells undergo premature replicative senescence. Heterozygotes are not known to exhibit any phenotype. (Weeda, 1997; PMID 9197240)

This mutation is also available on a predominantly C57BL/6-backcrossed genetic background (see Stock No. 040162), with homozygous animals reportedly surviving up to 38 days.

The donating laboratory wishes to note that all of their compound mutant experiments (PMID 27556946, PMID 36756698, PMID 38498063, PMID 22953029, PMID 38689513, PMID 38451018) were performed on an F1 hybrid genetic background. This hybrid background was derived from crosses of C57BL/6JOlaHsd-background mutant animals with FVB/NHanHsd-background mutant animals (e.g. Ercc1+/- FVB x Ercc1d/+C57BL/6 (Stock No. 040165)). The contributing single mutant alleles were maintained independently through crosses of heterozygotes with C57BL/6JOlaHsd or FVB/NHanHsd inbred mice rather than wildtype animals from within their colonies (e.g. Ercc1-/+ FVB x WT (Ercc1+/+) FVB). They did not maintain homozygous colonies and their F1 mice were not further intercrossed.

Browse References > Detailed Description D1-FlpO mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Drd1 (dopamine receptor 1) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Flp recombinase-dependent constructs to target Drd1-expressing cells and mark the direct pathway spiny projection neuronal subpopulation in striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 2 of the mouse Drd1 gene (ENSMUST00000021932.5) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO cassette using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: GAGATGAGAACCCAATATTCAGG). Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed at least 97.6% of the markers consistent with C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description D1-FlpO mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Drd1 (dopamine receptor 1) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Flp recombinase-dependent constructs to target Drd1-expressing cells and mark the direct pathway spiny projection neuronal subpopulation in striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 2 of the mouse Drd1 gene (ENSMUST00000021932.5) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO cassette using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: GAGATGAGAACCCAATATTCAGG). Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed at least 97.6% of the markers consistent with C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description Point mutations and duplications in the SNCA (synuclein, alpha) gene cause familial forms of Parkinson’s disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). The gene regulates vesicle exocytosis, but in the disease state forms insoluble deposits that cause extensive cytopathology and neuronal loss. WT-3877 mice express full-length human SNCA cDNA from the mouse Thy1.2 (Thy1, thymus cell antigen 1, theta) neuronal regulator promoter. Expression levels of SNCA are ~2-3 fold higher than endogenous levels in mouse. This strain can act as a control for 3K-3817 mutant mice (Stock No. 041612), which express similar levels of an SNCA transgene incorporating the E35K, E46K, and E61K mutations associated with Parkinson's disease. WT-3877 mice develop subtle Parkinson's disease phenotypes including gait differences (decreased velocity on a tread scan) at 12 months of age, and small-sized pan-neuronal phosphorylated-serine 129 (pS129) inclusions that are proteinase K-resistant at 6 months of age (PMIDs: 30308173, 32996158, 35445353). Read More Development Full-length human SNCA cDNA is under the control of the mouse Thy1 (thymus cell antigen 1, theta) promoter in this transgenic line. The transgene was microinjected into the pronucleus of C57BL/6J one-cell embryos. Founder line 3877 was subsequently established. The integration site and copy number of the transgene are unknown, but protein expression levels are ~2-3 times the endogenous mouse SNCA levels. Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6NCrl for 4-5 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). This strain can act as a control for 3K-3817 mutant mice (Stock No. 041612), which express similar levels of an SNCA transgene incorporating the E35K, E46K, and E61K mutations associated with Parkinson's disease. WT-3877 mice develop subtle Parkinson's disease phenotypes including gait differences (decreased velocity on a tread scan) at 12 months of age, and small-sized pan-neuronal phosphorylated-serine 129 (pS129) inclusions that are proteinase K-resistant at 6 months of age (PMIDs: 30308173, 32996158, 35445353). Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6NCrl for 4-5 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). Browse References > Detailed Description CAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3 transgenic mice have CAG promoter/enhancer sequences driving expression of a red fluorescent protein (RFP), an enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), and a microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 alpha (Map1lc3a or LC3) gene. LC3 serves as a marker for phagosomes in a wide variety of tissues. The dual expression of two fluorophores allows tracking of different types of phagocytic cellular compartments depending on the acidity of the environment. RFP is stable in acidic pH (pKa 4.5) while EGFP (pKa 5.9) is quenched in the acidic lysosomal environment, allowing autophagosomes to be distinguished from autolysosomes. Combined GFP and RFP fluorescence yields a yellow signal within high pH phagophores and autophagosomes, while EGFP is quenched in autolysosomes, and they emit only an RFP signal. Following ischemia-reperfusion injury, EGFP expression reaches a peak at 24 hours and returns to baseline levels at 3 days. Meanwhile, RFP expression also peaks at 24 hours but persists at high levels for 3 days before returning to baseline levels by 7 days. CAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3 mice are useful for studying the progression and recovery from ischemic injury in a variety of tissues. Hemizygotes are viable and fertile. The donating investigator did not try to make a homozygous colony. Read More Development TheCAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3transgene was designed with a human cytomegalovirus immediate early promoter enhancer with chicken beta-actin/rabbit beta-globin hybrid promoter (CAG; from the pCAGGS vector) driving expression of a red fluorescent protein (RFP), an enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), and a microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 alpha (Map1lc3aor LC3) gene. The transgene was microinjected into fertilized C57BL/6 oocytes and the donating investigator reported that founder mice were bred to C57BL/6 mice (see SNP note below). Upon arrival at The Jackson Laboratory, transgenic mice were bred to C57BL/6J inbred mice (Stock No.000664) to establish the colony. A 32 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 27 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. One of the 27 markers throughout the genome was segregating from an unknown source. All 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N were found to be segregating. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a C57BL/6N genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description CAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3 transgenic mice have CAG promoter/enhancer sequences driving expression of a red fluorescent protein (RFP), an enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), and a microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 alpha (Map1lc3a or LC3) gene. LC3 serves as a marker for phagosomes in a wide variety of tissues. The dual expression of two fluorophores allows tracking of different types of phagocytic cellular compartments depending on the acidity of the environment. RFP is stable in acidic pH (pKa 4.5) while EGFP (pKa 5.9) is quenched in the acidic lysosomal environment, allowing autophagosomes to be distinguished from autolysosomes. Combined GFP and RFP fluorescence yields a yellow signal within high pH phagophores and autophagosomes, while EGFP is quenched in autolysosomes, and they emit only an RFP signal. Following ischemia-reperfusion injury, EGFP expression reaches a peak at 24 hours and returns to baseline levels at 3 days. Meanwhile, RFP expression also peaks at 24 hours but persists at high levels for 3 days before returning to baseline levels by 7 days. CAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3 mice are useful for studying the progression and recovery from ischemic injury in a variety of tissues. Hemizygotes are viable and fertile. The donating investigator did not try to make a homozygous colony. The transgene was microinjected into fertilized C57BL/6 oocytes and the donating investigator reported that founder mice were bred to C57BL/6 mice (see SNP note below). Upon arrival at The Jackson Laboratory, transgenic mice were bred to C57BL/6J inbred mice (Stock No.000664) to establish the colony. A 32 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 27 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. One of the 27 markers throughout the genome was segregating from an unknown source. All 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N were found to be segregating. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a C57BL/6N genetic background. description: LRRK2 (leucine rich repeat kinase 2) protein contains a kinase domain where both the N2081D Crohn's disease (CD) risk and the G2019S Parkinson's disease (PD)-pathogenic variants are located. Lrrk2N2081D knock-in mice express the conserved N2081D LRRK2 variant, which is expressed at endogenous levels. Homozygotes show increased sensitivity to chemically-induced colitis. No pathological
phenotype: has been observed in untreated mice, however there is an increase in phosphorylated RAB10 (RAB10, member RAS oncogene family) protein levels in the tissues of these mice compared to wildtype. Rab10 encodes a key substrate for LRRK2. Colitis is induced by administering 2% dextran sodium sulfate (DSS) in the drinking water of 16-week-old homozygous male and female mice for 8 days, followed by 3 days of regular water for partial recovery. In both sexes, homozygous mice exhibit more severe weight loss compared to wildtype animals. A significant number of males require early sacrifice due to the severity of colitis symptoms. At the experimental end point, both male and female mice have shorter colons than their sex-matched wildtype counterparts, indicating a greater degree of colonic inflammation. Stool samples extracted from colons of N2081D mutation carriers have significantly higher levels of the proinflammatory marker lipocalin-2 (LCN2). Male N2081D carriers also have increased spleen weight compared to wildtype mice, suggesting a heightened immune response. Histological examination of colon samples reveals a greater degree of inflammation and tissue damage in both male and female Lrrk2N2081D carriers compared to sex-matched wildtype mice. Collectively, results show that the Lrrk2N2081D mutation significantly exacerbates colonic inflammation and the severity of induced colitis, validating the Lrrk2N2081D model as a tool to study Lrrk2-linked Crohn's disease pathogenic mechanisms. Studies suggest that the N2081D mutation activates LRRK2 by inducing a conformational shift, resulting in functional effects distinct from the Parkinson's disease-associated LRRK2 G2019S variant.
