development: An LRRK2 N2081D missense mutation (AAT->GAT) (conserved in both mouse and human) and a silent downstream mutation in an EcoRI site (GAGTTT->GAATTC) were introduced to exon 41 of the mouse Lrrk2 gene using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies. Single-stranded donor DNA was co-microinjected with gRNA (GCTAACTCATCAAACTCATTGG) and Cas9 protein into the pronuclei of C57BL/6J zygotes. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for approximately 3 or 4 generations to help remove any off-target mutations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025 (see SNP note and miniMUGA results below). Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. Cryorecovery/live colony development will involve C57BL/6J (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. One of the 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N was found to be segregating, the rd8 recessive mutation associated with retinal degeneration on Chromosome 1 within the Crb1 locus. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a mixed C57BL/6N;C57BL/6J genetic background. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed more than 99% of the markers as C57BL/6J and/or C57BL/6N. Additionally, 4 regions were identified having markers other than C57BL/6 present: Chromosome 3 ~52.76-53.52 Mb, Chromosome 3 ~53.88-56.82 Mb, Chromosome 12 ~73.63-87.89 Mb and Chromosome 19 ~59.11-59.53 Mb. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were C57BL/6-congenic (mixed C57BL/6N;C57BL/6J genetic background). Browse References > Detailed Description LRRK2 (leucine rich repeat kinase 2) protein contains a kinase domain where both the N2081D Crohn's disease (CD) risk and the G2019S Parkinson's disease (PD)-pathogenic variants are located. Lrrk2N2081D knock-in mice express the conserved N2081D LRRK2 variant, which is expressed at endogenous levels. Homozygotes show increased sensitivity to chemically-induced colitis. No pathological phenotype has been observed in untreated mice, however there is an increase in phosphorylated RAB10 (RAB10, member RAS oncogene family) protein levels in the tissues of these mice compared to wildtype. Rab10 encodes a key substrate for LRRK2. Colitis is induced by administering 2% dextran sodium sulfate (DSS) in the drinking water of 16-week-old homozygous male and female mice for 8 days, followed by 3 days of regular water for partial recovery. In both sexes, homozygous mice exhibit more severe weight loss compared to wildtype animals. A significant number of males require early sacrifice due to the severity of colitis symptoms. At the experimental end point, both male and female mice have shorter colons than their sex-matched wildtype counterparts, indicating a greater degree of colonic inflammation. Stool samples extracted from colons of N2081D mutation carriers have significantly higher levels of the proinflammatory marker lipocalin-2 (LCN2). Male N2081D carriers also have increased spleen weight compared to wildtype mice, suggesting a heightened immune response. Histological examination of colon samples reveals a greater degree of inflammation and tissue damage in both male and female Lrrk2N2081D carriers compared to sex-matched wildtype mice. Collectively, results show that the Lrrk2N2081D mutation significantly exacerbates colonic inflammation and the severity of induced colitis, validating the Lrrk2N2081D model as a tool to study Lrrk2-linked Crohn's disease pathogenic mechanisms. Studies suggest that the N2081D mutation activates LRRK2 by inducing a conformational shift, resulting in functional effects distinct from the Parkinson's disease-associated LRRK2 G2019S variant. Single-stranded donor DNA was co-microinjected with gRNA (GCTAACTCATCAAACTCATTGG) and Cas9 protein into the pronuclei of C57BL/6J zygotes. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for approximately 3 or 4 generations to help remove any off-target mutations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025 (see SNP note and miniMUGA results below). Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. Cryorecovery/live colony development will involve C57BL/6J (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. One of the 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N was found to be segregating, the rd8 recessive mutation associated with retinal degeneration on Chromosome 1 within the Crb1 locus. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a mixed C57BL/6N;C57BL/6J genetic background. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed more than 99% of the markers as C57BL/6J and/or C57BL/6N. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were C57BL/6-congenic (mixed C57BL/6N;C57BL/6J genetic background). development: To generate the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene, the 146 kb RPCI-1 human male P1 artificial chromosome (PAC) clone 27M07, containing the entire human SNCA (synuclein, alpha (non A4 component of amyloid precursor)) gene and 34 kb of its upstream region, was used. This transgene was microinjected into the pronuclei of fertilized FVB/N ova. The only transgenic founder shown to contain the complete SNCA gene was bred to FVB/N wildtype mice. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgenic mice were maintained as coisogenic on the FVB/N genetic background by
breeding: together as homozygotes. To generate the Snca knockout allele, a targeting vector was designed to replace exons 4 and 5 with a reverse-oriented neomycin resistance cassette (PGK-neo from the vector pPNT). The construct was electroporated into 129S6/SvEvTac-derived TC-1 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into recipient blastocysts and the resulting mutant mice were generated and maintained as coisogenic on the 129S6/SvEvTac genetic background. To generate the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- strain, mice homozygous for the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene (FVB/N genetic background) were bred with mice homozygous for the Snca knockout allele (129S6/SvEvTac genetic background). Double mutant mice were maintained on a mixed FVB/N;129S6/SvEvTac background using multiple breeding units without repeated brother-sister matings: thus the only portions of the FVB/N or 129S6/SvEvTac genomes fixed in these mice are the FVB/N regions flanking the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene insertion sites and the 129S6/SvEvTac regions around the Snca knockout allele. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice were sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository. Upon arrival, mice were bred together to establish the colony. Browse References > Detailed Description These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice are viable and fertile, harboring a Snca knockout allele and a transgene encoding the human α-synuclein. As homozygotes, expression of endogenous mouse α-synuclein is abolished and replaced by human α-synuclein from the two total insertions of the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT). While brain RNA expression of SNCAWT is more than 50-fold greater compared to normal endogenous mouse α-synuclein, protein levels are only 1 to 1.5-fold greater. In colon however, both RNA and protein expression of SNCAWT are ~100-fold greater than normal endogenous mouse α-synuclein. PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice do not show any enteric nervous system abnormalities or widespread α-synuclein aggregation in brain or colon. No detectable motor behavior impairments, autonomic abnormalities, olfactory dysfunction, dopaminergic deficits, Lewy body inclusions or neurodegeneration are associated with α-synuclein expression in these mice. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice are the experimental control for strains that model the very early gastrointestinal dysfunction in the absence of major central nervous system pathology seen in human Parkinson's disease (Stock Nos. 010788 and 010799). Read More Development To generate the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene, the 146 kb RPCI-1 human male P1 artificial chromosome (PAC) clone 27M07, containing the entire human SNCA (synuclein, alpha (non A4 component of amyloid precursor)) gene and 34 kb of its upstream region, was used. This transgene was microinjected into the pronuclei of fertilized FVB/N ova. The only transgenic founder shown to contain the complete SNCA gene was bred to FVB/N wildtype mice. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgenic mice were maintained as coisogenic on the FVB/N genetic background by breeding together as homozygotes. To generate the Snca knockout allele, a targeting vector was designed to replace exons 4 and 5 with a reverse-oriented neomycin resistance cassette (PGK-neo from the vector pPNT). The construct was electroporated into 129S6/SvEvTac-derived TC-1 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into recipient blastocysts and the resulting mutant mice were generated and maintained as coisogenic on the 129S6/SvEvTac genetic background. To generate the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- strain, mice homozygous for the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene (FVB/N genetic background) were bred with mice homozygous for the Snca knockout allele (129S6/SvEvTac genetic background). Double mutant mice were maintained on a mixed FVB/N;129S6/SvEvTac background using multiple breeding units without repeated brother-sister matings: thus the only portions of the FVB/N or 129S6/SvEvTac genomes fixed in these mice are the FVB/N regions flanking the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene insertion sites and the 129S6/SvEvTac regions around the Snca knockout allele. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice were sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository. Upon arrival, mice were bred together to establish the colony. Browse References > Detailed Description These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice are viable and fertile, harboring a Snca knockout allele and a transgene encoding the human α-synuclein. As homozygotes, expression of endogenous mouse α-synuclein is abolished and replaced by human α-synuclein from the two total insertions of the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT). While brain RNA expression of SNCAWT is more than 50-fold greater compared to normal endogenous mouse α-synuclein, protein levels are only 1 to 1.5-fold greater. In colon however, both RNA and protein expression of SNCAWT are ~100-fold greater than normal endogenous mouse α-synuclein. PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice do not show any enteric nervous system abnormalities or widespread α-synuclein aggregation in brain or colon. No detectable motor behavior impairments, autonomic abnormalities, olfactory dysfunction, dopaminergic deficits, Lewy body inclusions or neurodegeneration are associated with α-synuclein expression in these mice. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice are the experimental control for strains that model the very early gastrointestinal dysfunction in the absence of major central nervous system pathology seen in human Parkinson's disease (Stock Nos. 010788 and 010799). Read More Development To generate the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene, the 146 kb RPCI-1 human male P1 artificial chromosome (PAC) clone 27M07, containing the entire human SNCA (synuclein, alpha (non A4 component of amyloid precursor)) gene and 34 kb of its upstream region, was used. This transgene was microinjected into the pronuclei of fertilized FVB/N ova. The only transgenic founder shown to contain the complete SNCA gene was bred to FVB/N wildtype mice. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgenic mice were maintained as coisogenic on the FVB/N genetic background by breeding together as homozygotes. To generate the Snca knockout allele, a targeting vector was designed to replace exons 4 and 5 with a reverse-oriented neomycin resistance cassette (PGK-neo from the vector pPNT). The construct was electroporated into 129S6/SvEvTac-derived TC-1 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into recipient blastocysts and the resulting mutant mice were generated and maintained as coisogenic on the 129S6/SvEvTac genetic background. To generate the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- strain, mice homozygous for the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene (FVB/N genetic background) were bred with mice homozygous for the Snca knockout allele (129S6/SvEvTac genetic background). Double mutant mice were maintained on a mixed FVB/N;129S6/SvEvTac background using multiple breeding units without repeated brother-sister matings: thus the only portions of the FVB/N or 129S6/SvEvTac genomes fixed in these mice are the FVB/N regions flanking the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene insertion sites and the 129S6/SvEvTac regions around the Snca knockout allele. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice were sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository. Upon arrival, mice were bred together to establish the colony. Browse References > Detailed Description These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice are viable and fertile, harboring a Snca knockout allele and a transgene encoding the human α-synuclein. As homozygotes, expression of endogenous mouse α-synuclein is abolished and replaced by human α-synuclein from the two total insertions of the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT). While brain RNA expression of SNCAWT is more than 50-fold greater compared to normal endogenous mouse α-synuclein, protein levels are only 1 to 1.5-fold greater. In colon however, both RNA and protein expression of SNCAWT are ~100-fold greater than normal endogenous mouse α-synuclein. PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice do not show any enteric nervous system abnormalities or widespread α-synuclein aggregation in brain or colon. No detectable motor behavior impairments, autonomic abnormalities, olfactory dysfunction, dopaminergic deficits, Lewy body inclusions or neurodegeneration are associated with α-synuclein expression in these mice. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice are the experimental control for strains that model the very early gastrointestinal dysfunction in the absence of major central nervous system pathology seen in human Parkinson's disease (Stock Nos. 010788 and 010799). Read More Development To generate the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene, the 146 kb RPCI-1 human male P1 artificial chromosome (PAC) clone 27M07, containing the entire human SNCA (synuclein, alpha (non A4 component of amyloid precursor)) gene and 34 kb of its upstream region, was used. This transgene was microinjected into the pronuclei of fertilized FVB/N ova. The only transgenic founder shown to contain the complete SNCA gene was bred to FVB/N wildtype mice. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgenic mice were maintained as coisogenic on the FVB/N genetic background by breeding together as homozygotes. To generate the Snca knockout allele, a targeting vector was designed to replace exons 4 and 5 with a reverse-oriented neomycin resistance cassette (PGK-neo from the vector pPNT). The construct was electroporated into 129S6/SvEvTac-derived TC-1 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into recipient blastocysts and the resulting mutant mice were generated and maintained as coisogenic on the 129S6/SvEvTac genetic background. To generate the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- strain, mice homozygous for the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene (FVB/N genetic background) were bred with mice homozygous for the Snca knockout allele (129S6/SvEvTac genetic background). Double mutant mice were maintained on a mixed FVB/N;129S6/SvEvTac background using multiple breeding units without repeated brother-sister matings: thus the only portions of the FVB/N or 129S6/SvEvTac genomes fixed in these mice are the FVB/N regions flanking the PAC-Tg(SNCAWT) transgene insertion sites and the 129S6/SvEvTac regions around the Snca knockout allele. These PAC-Tg(SNCAWT);Snca-/- mice were sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository. Upon arrival, mice were bred together to establish the colony. description: These M83 transgenic mice express human A53T variant alpha-synuclein (full-length, 140 amino acid isoform) under the direction of the mouse prion protein promoter. Mice homozygous for the transgenic insert are viable, fertile and normal in size. At eight months of age, some homozygous mice develop a progressively severe motor
phenotype: . Presentation of the phenotype may manifest at 14-15 months of age (on average). Lax grooming, weight loss and diminished mobility precede movement impairment, partial limb paralysis, trembling and inability to stand. Immunohistochemistry analysis of mutants between eight to 12 months of age reveals widely distributed alpha-synuclein inclusions, with dense accumulation in the spinal cord, brainstem, cerebellum and thalamus. The appearance of alpha-synuclein aggregate inclusions parallels the onset of the motor impairment phenotype. Axons and myelin sheaths exhibit progressive ultrastructural degeneration. Immunoelectron microscopy and biochemical analysis show the inclusions in neurons are comprised primarily of 10-16 nm fibrils of alpha-synuclein. The structure, location and onset of the inclusions seen in the mutant mice resemble characteristics seen in human neuronal alpha-synucleinopathies, such as familial Parkinson's Disease. In addition, mice exhibit impaired odor discrimination and detection beginning at 6 months of age. Homozygous mice have a high incidence of nonproductive matings. Aggression is observed, particularly in males, and may be due at least in part to the B6;C3H genetic background. Mice hemizygous for the transgenic insert develop similar phenotypic traits, but onset occurs later, between 22 and 28 months of age. Mice homozygous for the transgenic insert are viable, fertile and normal in size. At eight months of age, some homozygous mice develop a progressively severe motor phenotype. Presentation of the phenotype may manifest at 14-15 months of age (on average). Lax grooming, weight loss and diminished mobility precede movement impairment, partial limb paralysis, trembling and inability to stand. Immunohistochemistry analysis of mutants between eight to 12 months of age reveals widely distributed alpha-synuclein inclusions, with dense accumulation in the spinal cord, brainstem, cerebellum and thalamus. The appearance of alpha-synuclein aggregate inclusions parallels the onset of the motor impairment phenotype. Axons and myelin sheaths exhibit progressive ultrastructural degeneration. Immunoelectron microscopy and biochemical analysis show the inclusions in neurons are comprised primarily of 10-16 nm fibrils of alpha-synuclein. The structure, location and onset of the inclusions seen in the mutant mice resemble characteristics seen in human neuronal alpha-synucleinopathies, such as familial Parkinson's Disease. In addition, mice exhibit impaired odor discrimination and detection beginning at 6 months of age. Homozygous mice have a high incidence of nonproductive matings. When hemizygotes are bred together, there may be some incidence of nonproductive matings (~20%). Aggression is observed, particularly in males, and may be due at least in part to the B6;C3H genetic background. Read More. Phenotype: . Presentation of the phenotype may manifest at 14-15 months of age (on average). Lax grooming, weight loss and diminished mobility precede movement impairment, partial limb paralysis, trembling and inability to stand. Immunohistochemistry analysis of mutants between eight to 12 months of age reveals widely distributed alpha-synuclein inclusions, with dense accumulation in the spinal cord, brainstem, cerebellum and thalamus. The appearance of alpha-synuclein aggregate inclusions parallels the onset of the motor impairment phenotype. Axons and myelin sheaths exhibit progressive ultrastructural degeneration. Immunoelectron microscopy and biochemical analysis show the inclusions in neurons are comprised primarily of 10-16 nm fibrils of alpha-synuclein. development: A targeting vector was designed to replace exon 5 and part of exon 4 encoding the nuclear factor, erythroid derived 2, like 2 (Nfe2l2) gene with a β-galactosidase (lacZ) reporter followed by a neomycin resistance (neo) cassette and a polyadenylation sequence. The construct was electroporated into 129X1/SvJ-derived JM-1 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts and the resulting chimeric mice were bred to C57BL/6 mice to generate a colony of Nrf2-/- mice. The donating investigator reported that these mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J (see SNP note below) for at least 10 generations . Upon arrival at The Jackson Laboratory, mice were bred to C57BL/6J (Stock No. 000664) for at least one generation. In 2018, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. One of the 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N was found to be segregating. This marker is the rd8 recessive mutation associated with retinal degeneration on Chromosome 1 within the Crb1 locus. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a mixed C57BL/6N;C57BL/6J genetic background. development: A targeting vector was designed to replace exon 5 and part of exon 4 encoding the nuclear factor, erythroid derived 2, like 2 (Nfe2l2) gene with a β-galactosidase (lacZ) reporter followed by a neomycin resistance (neo) cassette and a polyadenylation sequence. The construct was electroporated into 129X1/SvJ-derived JM-1 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts and the resulting chimeric mice were bred to C57BL/6 mice to generate a colony of Nrf2-/- mice. The donating investigator reported that these mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J (see SNP note below) for at least 10 generations . Upon arrival at The Jackson Laboratory, mice were bred to C57BL/6J (Stock No. 000664) for at least one generation. In 2018, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. One of the 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N was found to be segregating. This marker is the rd8 recessive mutation associated with retinal degeneration on Chromosome 1 within the Crb1 locus. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a mixed C57BL/6N;C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description In this NRF2 knockout strain, a β-galactosidase (lacZ) reporter followed by a neomycin resistance (neo) cassette replaces exon 5 and part of exon 4 encoding the nuclear factor, erythroid derived 2, like 2 gene (Nfe2l2) gene, abolishing gene function. Homozygotes are viable, fertile, and normal in size. NRF2, a member of the "cap 'n' collar" (CNC) subfamily of the basic region-leucine zipper transcription factors, is a regulator of endogenous antioxidant protection, microglial function, and chronic neuroinflammation. Inactivation of the CNC, DNA binding, and leucine zipper domains in Nrf2-/- mice results in age-related macular degeneration (AMD)-like retinal pathology, spontaneous choroidal neovascularization (CNV), increased sensitivity to toxins, impaired adipogenesis, abnormal mitochondria, and an increase in proinflammatory gene expression in microglia and astrocytes. The donating investigator reports that lacZ failed to generate any detectable β-galactosidase activity. Read More Development A targeting vector was designed to replace exon 5 and part of exon 4 encoding the nuclear factor, erythroid derived 2, like 2 (Nfe2l2) gene with a β-galactosidase (lacZ) reporter followed by a neomycin resistance (neo) cassette and a polyadenylation sequence. The construct was electroporated into 129X1/SvJ-derived JM-1 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts and the resulting chimeric mice were bred to C57BL/6 mice to generate a colony of Nrf2-/- mice. The donating investigator reported that these mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J (see SNP note below) for at least 10 generations . Upon arrival at The Jackson Laboratory, mice were bred to C57BL/6J (Stock No. 000664) for at least one generation. In 2018, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. One of the 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N was found to be segregating. This marker is the rd8 recessive mutation associated with retinal degeneration on Chromosome 1 within the Crb1 locus. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a mixed C57BL/6N;C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description Mice homozygous for this dopamine transporter IRES-cre (DATIREScre) knock-in allele are viable and fertile. Cre recombinase activity is observed as early as embryonic day 15, and co-localizes with endogenous gene expression in adult dopaminergic cell groups (substantia nigra (SN) and ventral tegmental area (VTA), as well as in the retrorubral field). Lesser Cre recombinase activity occurs in adult olfactory bulb glomeruli, mimicking the known lowerSlc6a3(or DAT) expression in this tissue. Although the pattern and intensity of DAT immunostaining in the SN, VTA and striatum do not differ between wild-type and mutant mice, striatum DAT protein levels are moderately reduced (17%) in heterozygotes and significantly reduced (47%) in homozygotes. This diminution in homozygous striatum is associated with significantly increased neuropeptide PDyn (but not D1, D2, or PPE) mRNA levels compared to wild-type, while such an increase is not observed in heterozygotes. When bred with mice containing aloxP-flanked sequence of interest, Cre-mediated recombination will result in deletion of the flanked genome in dopaminergic neurons. As such, these mutant mice may be useful in neurobiological studies to facilitate the analysis of gene function in dopaminergic neurons, such as drug addiction or Parkinson's disease. In an attempt to offer alleles on well-characterized or multiple genetic backgrounds, alleles are frequently moved to a genetic background different from that on which an allele was first characterized. It should be noted that the phenotype could vary from that originally described. The strain description will be modified as published results become available. Browse References > Detailed Description Mice homozygous for this dopamine transporter IRES-cre (DATIREScre) knock-in allele are viable and fertile. Cre recombinase activity is observed as early as embryonic day 15, and co-localizes with endogenous gene expression in adult dopaminergic cell groups (substantia nigra (SN) and ventral tegmental area (VTA), as well as in the retrorubral field). Lesser Cre recombinase activity occurs in adult olfactory bulb glomeruli, mimicking the known lowerSlc6a3(or DAT) expression in this tissue. Although the pattern and intensity of DAT immunostaining in the SN, VTA and striatum do not differ between wild-type and mutant mice, striatum DAT protein levels are moderately reduced (17%) in heterozygotes and significantly reduced (47%) in homozygotes. This diminution in homozygous striatum is associated with significantly increased neuropeptide PDyn (but not D1, D2, or PPE) mRNA levels compared to wild-type, while such an increase is not observed in heterozygotes. When bred with mice containing aloxP-flanked sequence of interest, Cre-mediated recombination will result in deletion of the flanked genome in dopaminergic neurons. As such, these mutant mice may be useful in neurobiological studies to facilitate the analysis of gene function in dopaminergic neurons, such as drug addiction or Parkinson's disease. In an attempt to offer alleles on well-characterized or multiple genetic backgrounds, alleles are frequently moved to a genetic background different from that on which an allele was first characterized. It should be noted that the phenotype could vary from that originally described. The strain description will be modified as published results become available. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6-derived CMT2 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts and chimeric mice were bred to C57BL/6 mice. The FRT-flanked neo cassette was removed in the germline mice by intercrossing with a Flpe-deleter strain on a mixed B6;SJL background (see Stock No. 003800). The resulting mutant offspring (now harboring this DATIREScre allele) were maintained on this mixed genetic background prior to arrival at The Jackson Laboratory. Browse References > Detailed Description Mice homozygous for this dopamine transporter IRES-cre (DATIREScre) knock-in allele are viable and fertile. Cre recombinase activity is observed as early as embryonic day 15, and co-localizes with endogenous gene expression in adult dopaminergic cell groups (substantia nigra (SN) and ventral tegmental area (VTA), as well as in the retrorubral field). Lesser Cre recombinase activity occurs in adult olfactory bulb glomeruli, mimicking the known lowerSlc6a3(or DAT) expression in this tissue. Although the pattern and intensity of DAT immunostaining in the SN, VTA and striatum do not differ between wild-type and mutant mice, striatum DAT protein levels are moderately reduced (17%) in heterozygotes and significantly reduced (47%) in homozygotes. This diminution in homozygous striatum is associated with significantly increased neuropeptide PDyn (but not D1, D2, or PPE) mRNA levels compared to wild-type, while such an increase is not observed in heterozygotes. When bred with mice containing aloxP-flanked sequence of interest, Cre-mediated recombination will result in deletion of the flanked genome in dopaminergic neurons. As such, these mutant mice may be useful in neurobiological studies to facilitate the analysis of gene function in dopaminergic neurons, such as drug addiction or Parkinson's disease. In an attempt to offer alleles on well-characterized or multiple genetic backgrounds, alleles are frequently moved to a genetic background different from that on which an allele was first characterized. It should be noted that the phenotype could vary from that originally described. The strain description will be modified as published results become available. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6-derived CMT2 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts and chimeric mice were bred to C57BL/6 mice. The FRT-flanked neo cassette was removed in the germline mice by intercrossing with a Flpe-deleter strain on a mixed B6;SJL background (see Stock No. 003800). The resulting mutant offspring (now harboring this DATIREScre allele) were maintained on this mixed genetic background prior to arrival at The Jackson Laboratory. Upon arrival, mice were backcrossed to the C57BL/6J inbred strain (Stock No. 000664) for at least five generations. Browse References > Detailed Description Mice homozygous for this dopamine transporter IRES-cre (DATIREScre) knock-in allele are viable and fertile. Cre recombinase activity is observed as early as embryonic day 15, and co-localizes with endogenous gene expression in adult dopaminergic cell groups (substantia nigra (SN) and ventral tegmental area (VTA), as well as in the retrorubral field). Lesser Cre recombinase activity occurs in adult olfactory bulb glomeruli, mimicking the known lowerSlc6a3(or DAT) expression in this tissue. Although the pattern and intensity of DAT immunostaining in the SN, VTA and striatum do not differ between wild-type and mutant mice, striatum DAT protein levels are moderately reduced (17%) in heterozygotes and significantly reduced (47%) in homozygotes. This diminution in homozygous striatum is associated with significantly increased neuropeptide PDyn (but not D1, D2, or PPE) mRNA levels compared to wild-type, while such an increase is not observed in heterozygotes. When bred with mice containing aloxP-flanked sequence of interest, Cre-mediated recombination will result in deletion of the flanked genome in dopaminergic neurons. As such, these mutant mice may be useful in neurobiological studies to facilitate the analysis of gene function in dopaminergic neurons, such as drug addiction or Parkinson's disease. In an attempt to offer alleles on well-characterized or multiple genetic backgrounds, alleles are frequently moved to a genetic background different from that on which an allele was first characterized. It should be noted that the phenotype could vary from that originally described. The strain description will be modified as published results become available. development: Exon 8 (NM_001077411.4) of the mouse Gba1 gene was modified using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies to incorporate an E344K (GAG->AAG) knock-in (bold) and 3 silent mutations (lower case): wildtype CCAAAGCTACTTTAGGAGAGACA to mutant CtAAgGCcACTTTAGGAAAGACA. SgRNA TGTCTCTCCTAAAGTAGCTT, donor DNA, and Cas9 mRNA were injected into hybrid embryos (MF1 outbred ; C57BL/6 inbred). The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 8 generations (see SNP note below). The donating laboratory sent 2 homozygous males (black coat color) to The Jackson Laboratory in 2022. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2022, a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (~9000 SNP) analysis was performed on the 2 males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. These data showed ~97-99% C57BL/6 markers (~89-92% C57BL/6J ; ~7-8% C57BL/6NCrl). The remaining 1-3% of the markers were of unknown origin, which may represent MF1 outbred contribution from the embryos used in creating the mice. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J. Browse References > Detailed Description The E326K coding variant (current nomenclature E365K) of the human GBA1 (glucosidase, beta, acid 1) gene on chromosome 1q22 is potentially associated with increased susceptibility to familial Parkinson's disease (PMID:28830825). Gba1E326K mice carry a corresponding E344K (GAG to AAG) knock-in and 2 silent mutations in exon 8 of the mouse Gba1 gene. Homozygotes show ~30-40% reduction in GCase activity in whole brain tissue as well as a decrease in the total protein. They are viable and fertile and without overt phenotype. This strain has not as yet been published and studies are ongoing. We will update this description as more information becomes known. (February, 2022) Distribution of this strain was supported by the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research. SgRNA TGTCTCTCCTAAAGTAGCTT, donor DNA, and Cas9 mRNA were injected into hybrid embryos (MF1 outbred ; C57BL/6 inbred). The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 8 generations (see SNP note below). The donating laboratory sent 2 homozygous males (black coat color) to The Jackson Laboratory in 2022. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2022, a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (~9000 SNP) analysis was performed on the 2 males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. These data showed ~97-99% C57BL/6 markers (~89-92% C57BL/6J ; ~7-8% C57BL/6NCrl). The remaining 1-3% of the markers were of unknown origin, which may represent MF1 outbred contribution from the embryos used in creating the mice. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J. Browse References > Detailed Description In Parkinson's disease, dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the midbrain gradually degenerate, with ventral substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) DANs exhibiting greater vulnerability. Slc6a3 (solute carrier family 6 (neurotransmitter transporter, dopamine), member 3; also called DAT) encodes a dopamine transporter protein and is expressed in dopaminergic neurons. DAT-FlpO (also called DAT-Flp or Slc6a3-T2A-FlpO) mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Slc6a3 promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. When crossed with animals carrying FRT-flanked sequences, the FRT'ed region is excised in Slc6a3-expressing cells of the offspring. Characterization of the DAT-FlpO line expression and examination of whole-brain efferent and afferent connectivity of dopaminergic neuron subtypes was accomplished through crosses with an unspecified Ai65 Flp reporter line. TdTomato+ cells were confirmed to be tyrosine hydroxylase positive (TH+) neurons. (Fushiki, 2024; PMID 39763754) Read More Development The TAA stop codon in exon 15 of the mouse Slc6a3 gene (ENSMUST00000022100.6) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO-rBG (rabbit β-globin polyadenylation signal)-pA cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: CCAACAGCCAATGGCGCAGCTGG). Two silent mutations aa.613 L(CTG to TTA), aa.614 R(CGC to AGG) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed 100% of the markers consistent with C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description In Parkinson's disease, dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the midbrain gradually degenerate, with ventral substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) DANs exhibiting greater vulnerability. Slc6a3 (solute carrier family 6 (neurotransmitter transporter, dopamine), member 3; also called DAT) encodes a dopamine transporter protein and is expressed in dopaminergic neurons. DAT-FlpO (also called DAT-Flp or Slc6a3-T2A-FlpO) mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Slc6a3 promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. When crossed with animals carrying FRT-flanked sequences, the FRT'ed region is excised in Slc6a3-expressing cells of the offspring. Characterization of the DAT-FlpO line expression and examination of whole-brain efferent and afferent connectivity of dopaminergic neuron subtypes was accomplished through crosses with an unspecified Ai65 Flp reporter line. TdTomato+ cells were confirmed to be tyrosine hydroxylase positive (TH+) neurons. (Fushiki, 2024; PMID 39763754) Read More Development The TAA stop codon in exon 15 of the mouse Slc6a3 gene (ENSMUST00000022100.6) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO-rBG (rabbit β-globin polyadenylation signal)-pA cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: CCAACAGCCAATGGCGCAGCTGG). Two silent mutations aa.613 L(CTG to TTA), aa.614 R(CGC to AGG) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed 100% of the markers consistent with C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description In Parkinson's disease, dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the midbrain gradually degenerate, with ventral substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) DANs exhibiting greater vulnerability. Slc6a3 (solute carrier family 6 (neurotransmitter transporter, dopamine), member 3; also called DAT) encodes a dopamine transporter protein and is expressed in dopaminergic neurons. DAT-FlpO (also called DAT-Flp or Slc6a3-T2A-FlpO) mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Slc6a3 promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. When crossed with animals carrying FRT-flanked sequences, the FRT'ed region is excised in Slc6a3-expressing cells of the offspring. Characterization of the DAT-FlpO line expression and examination of whole-brain efferent and afferent connectivity of dopaminergic neuron subtypes was accomplished through crosses with an unspecified Ai65 Flp reporter line. TdTomato+ cells were confirmed to be tyrosine hydroxylase positive (TH+) neurons. (Fushiki, 2024; PMID 39763754) Read More Development The TAA stop codon in exon 15 of the mouse Slc6a3 gene (ENSMUST00000022100.6) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO-rBG (rabbit β-globin polyadenylation signal)-pA cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: CCAACAGCCAATGGCGCAGCTGG). Two silent mutations aa.613 L(CTG to TTA), aa.614 R(CGC to AGG) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed 100% of the markers consistent with C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description In Parkinson's disease, dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the midbrain gradually degenerate, with ventral substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) DANs exhibiting greater vulnerability. Slc6a3 (solute carrier family 6 (neurotransmitter transporter, dopamine), member 3; also called DAT) encodes a dopamine transporter protein and is expressed in dopaminergic neurons. DAT-FlpO (also called DAT-Flp or Slc6a3-T2A-FlpO) mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Slc6a3 promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. When crossed with animals carrying FRT-flanked sequences, the FRT'ed region is excised in Slc6a3-expressing cells of the offspring. Characterization of the DAT-FlpO line expression and examination of whole-brain efferent and afferent connectivity of dopaminergic neuron subtypes was accomplished through crosses with an unspecified Ai65 Flp reporter line. TdTomato+ cells were confirmed to be tyrosine hydroxylase positive (TH+) neurons. (Fushiki, 2024; PMID 39763754) Read More Development The TAA stop codon in exon 15 of the mouse Slc6a3 gene (ENSMUST00000022100.6) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO-rBG (rabbit β-globin polyadenylation signal)-pA cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: CCAACAGCCAATGGCGCAGCTGG). Two silent mutations aa.613 L(CTG to TTA), aa.614 R(CGC to AGG) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed 100% of the markers consistent with C57BL/6J genetic background. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Cre recombinase-dependent constructs to target Adora2a-expressing cells and the dopamine 2 (D2)/adenosine A2a receptor neuronal subpopulation that marks the indirect pathway of the striatum. They offer a fully characterized alternative to existing BAC transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), Dr-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). Browse References > Detailed Description A2a-Cre mice express Cre recombinase from the mouse Adora2a (adenosine A2a receptor) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Cre recombinase-dependent constructs to target Adora2a-expressing cells and the dopamine 2 (D2)/adenosine A2a receptor neuronal subpopulation that marks the indirect pathway of the striatum. They offer a fully characterized alternative to existing BAC transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), Dr-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Two synonymous mutations, p.A394 (GCC to GCA) and p.R397 (AGG to CGC), were also introduced to exon 3 to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for 4 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). Browse References > Detailed Description A2a-Cre mice express Cre recombinase from the mouse Adora2a (adenosine A2a receptor) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Cre recombinase-dependent constructs to target Adora2a-expressing cells and the dopamine 2 (D2)/adenosine A2a receptor neuronal subpopulation that marks the indirect pathway of the striatum. They offer a fully characterized alternative to existing BAC transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), Dr-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 3 of the mouse Adora2a gene (ENSMUST00000105420) on mouse Chromosome 10 was replaced with a T2A-Cre cassette using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: AGGCTGTTCCTACCCTACCCTGG). Two synonymous mutations, p.A394 (GCC to GCA) and p.R397 (AGG to CGC), were also introduced to exon 3 to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for 4 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). Browse References > Detailed Description A2a-FlpO mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Adora2a (adenosine A2a receptor) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Flp recombinase-dependent constructs to target Adora2a-expressing cells and the dopamine 2 (D2)/adenosine A2a receptor neuronal subpopulation that marks the indirect pathway of the striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 3 of the mouse Adora2a gene (ENSMUST00000105420.2) on mouse Chromosome 10 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO cassette using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: AGGCTGTTCCTACCCTACCCTGG). Two silent mutations (aa. 394A (GCC to GCA) and aa. 397R (AGG to CGC)) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed at least 97.1% of the markers as C57BL/6J. Additionally, one region was identified having markers other than C57BL/6 present on Chromosome 10 ~48.6-75.6 Mb (likely reflecting the Adora2a-T2A-FlpO mutation at Chromosome 10 ~75 Mb). These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were on a C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description A2a-FlpO mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Adora2a (adenosine A2a receptor) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Flp recombinase-dependent constructs to target Adora2a-expressing cells and the dopamine 2 (D2)/adenosine A2a receptor neuronal subpopulation that marks the indirect pathway of the striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 3 of the mouse Adora2a gene (ENSMUST00000105420.2) on mouse Chromosome 10 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO cassette using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: AGGCTGTTCCTACCCTACCCTGG). Two silent mutations (aa. 394A (GCC to GCA) and aa. 397R (AGG to CGC)) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed at least 97.1% of the markers as C57BL/6J. Additionally, one region was identified having markers other than C57BL/6 present on Chromosome 10 ~48.6-75.6 Mb (likely reflecting the Adora2a-T2A-FlpO mutation at Chromosome 10 ~75 Mb). These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were on a C57BL/6J genetic background. Browse References > Detailed Description A2a-FlpO mice express optimized Flp recombinase (FlpO) from the mouse Adora2a (adenosine A2a receptor) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Flp recombinase-dependent constructs to target Adora2a-expressing cells and the dopamine 2 (D2)/adenosine A2a receptor neuronal subpopulation that marks the indirect pathway of the striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 3 of the mouse Adora2a gene (ENSMUST00000105420.2) on mouse Chromosome 10 was replaced with a T2A-FlpO cassette using CRISPR/Cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: AGGCTGTTCCTACCCTACCCTGG). Two silent mutations (aa. 394A (GCC to GCA) and aa. 397R (AGG to CGC)) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. The donating laboratory reported the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 10 generations prior to sending heterozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the first generation rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6J allele-type. In 2025, the heterozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed at least 97.1% of the markers as C57BL/6J. Additionally, one region was identified having markers other than C57BL/6 present on Chromosome 10 ~48.6-75.6 Mb (likely reflecting the Adora2a-T2A-FlpO mutation at Chromosome 10 ~75 Mb). These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were on a C57BL/6J genetic background. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Flp recombinase-dependent constructs to target Adora2a-expressing cells and the dopamine 2 (D2)/adenosine A2a receptor neuronal subpopulation that marks the indirect pathway of the striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). Two silent mutations (aa. 394A (GCC to GCA) and aa. 397R (AGG to CGC)) were introduced to prevent the binding and re-cutting of the sequence by gRNA after homology-directed repair. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. description: Mutations in human GBA1 (glucosidase, beta, acid 1) can cause Gaucher disease, an autosomal recessive lysosomal (lipid) storage disease, and have been associated with late onset Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia. These mice express the mutant D427V Gba1 protein, which corresponds to the D409V mutation in the mature human GBA1 protein, and possess loxP sites flanking exons 6 through 8. Mice that are heterozygous for the targeted mutation are viable and fertile. Homozygous Gba1 D409V knock-in mice show a significant reduction in Gba1 protein level and glucocerebrosidase activity, and a significant increase in glucosylsphingosine in both brain and liver tissues. Heterozygotes demonstrate significant cognitive impairment by the age of 12 months, as determined by both Morris water maze and Y-maze behavioral tests (PMID: 31299418). When these mutant mice are bred to mice that express Cre recombinase, resulting offspring will have exons 6 through 8 deleted in the cre-expressing tissues and will no longer express the mutant D427V protein. Preliminary characterization was presented in a poster at the 2015 Society for Neuroscience conference. Read More

development: A targeting vector containing a FRT site flanked NEO cassette, and a F3 FRT site flanked PurO cassette was used to introduce the D427V point mutation into exon 10. The FRT site flanked NEO cassette was inserted into intron 5 and the F3 FRT site flanked PurO cassette was inserted into intron 8. In addition, loxP sites were inserted to flank exons 6 through 8. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6NTac derived Art B6 3.6 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into BALB/c blastocysts. The resulting chimeric animals were crossed to FLP recombinase expressing females on the C57BL/6NTac background, C57BL/6NTac-Tg(CAG-Flpe)2Art, to remove the selection cassettes (see SNP results below). These mice no longer carry the FLP recombinase allele. Upon arrival at The Jackson Laboratory, the mice were crossed to C57BL/6N (Stock No. 005304) at least once to establish the colony. A 32 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 27 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. While the 27 markers throughout the genome suggested a C57BL/6 genetic background, 4 of 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N were found to be segregating. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a mixed C57BL/6J ; C57BL/6N genetic background. Mutations in human GBA1 (glucosidase, beta, acid 1) can cause Gaucher disease, an autosomal recessive lysosomal (lipid) storage disease, and have been associated with late onset Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia. These mice express the mutant D427V Gba1 protein, which corresponds to the D409V mutation in the mature human GBA1 protein, and possess loxP sites flanking exons 6 through 8. Mice that are heterozygous for the targeted mutation are viable and fertile. Homozygous Gba1 D409V knock-in mice show a significant reduction in Gba1 protein level and glucocerebrosidase activity, and a significant increase in glucosylsphingosine in both brain and liver tissues.

Heterozygotes demonstrate significant cognitive impairment by the age of 12 months, as determined by both Morris water maze and Y-maze behavioral tests (PMID: 31299418).

When these mutant mice are bred to mice that express Cre recombinase, resulting offspring will have exons 6 through 8 deleted in the cre-expressing tissues and will no longer express the mutant D427V protein.

Preliminary characterization was presented in a poster at the 2015 Society for Neuroscience conference.

A 32 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 27 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. Browse References > Detailed Description D1-Cre mice express Cre recombinase from the mouse Drd1 (dopamine receptor 1) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Cre recombinase-dependent constructs to target Drd1-expressing cells and mark the direct pathway spiny projection neuronal subpopulation in striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. They offer a fully characterized alternative to existing BAC transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 2 of the mouse Drd1 gene (ENSMUT00000021932) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-Cre cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: GAGATGAGAACCCAATATTCAGG). Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 5 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Cre recombinase-dependent constructs to target Drd1-expressing cells and mark the direct pathway spiny projection neuronal subpopulation in striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. They offer a fully characterized alternative to existing BAC transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 2 of the mouse Drd1 gene (ENSMUT00000021932) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-Cre cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: GAGATGAGAACCCAATATTCAGG). Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 5 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). Browse References > Detailed Description D1-Cre mice express Cre recombinase from the mouse Drd1 (dopamine receptor 1) promoter. Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted by the knock-in mutation. This line can be combined with viral vectors or mouse lines expressing Cre recombinase-dependent constructs to target Drd1-expressing cells and mark the direct pathway spiny projection neuronal subpopulation in striatum. Heterozygous mice demonstrate no overt phenotype and are fertile. They offer a fully characterized alternative to existing BAC transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. A series of knock-in lines were created by the donating laboratory using a similar targeting strategy to allow direct expression comparisons: A2a-Cre (Stock No. 040186), A2a-FlpO (Stock No. 040187), D1-Cre (Stock No. 040188), and D1-FlpO (Stock No. 040189). The availability of both Cre- and FlpO-expressing alleles controlled from Adora2a (A2a) and Drd1 (dopamine receptor D1) promoters permits the simultaneous but independent examination of both the indirect and direct striatal pathway subpopulations, respectively, during disease progression. Read More Development The TGA stop codon in exon 2 of the mouse Drd1 gene (ENSMUT00000021932) on mouse Chromosome 13 was replaced with a T2A-Cre cassette using CRISPR/cas9 methodologies in C57BL/6N embryos (gRNA: GAGATGAGAACCCAATATTCAGG). Expression of the targeted gene is not disrupted. Resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J for more than 5 generations by the donating laboratory. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish a live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). Browse References > Detailed Description α-Synuclein is a neuronal protein (coded by Snca) which plays a role in synaptic plasticity and neurotransmitter release. Mutations of Snca have been implicated in a group of neurodegenerative diseases that result from an accumulation of α-synuclein in neurons or, in some cases, glial cells. These disorders include Parkinson's disease (PDD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), the Lewy body variant of Alzheimer's disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation. These humanized A53T SNCA-GR (gene replacement) knock-in/knock-out mice carry a 158 kb fragment of human SNCA replacing the mouse Snca locus and the pathogenic A53T mutation (alanine to threonine) associated with early -onset Parkinson's disease. Mice homozygous for the mutation are viable and fertile with no obvious phenotype. These mice may be useful for studying SNCA function. Of note, the SNCA-GR model set also includes: B6J.B6N-Sncatm1.1(SNCA)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039166) and B6J.B6N-Sncatm3.1(SNCA*E46K)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039168). Read More Development The A53T SNCA-GR targeting vector was designed to insert a 158 kb (Chr4:89,707,185-89,865,027) fragment of the human SNCA (synuclein, alpha) carrying the A53T (alanine to threonine) mutation in place of Chr6:60,683,985-60,848,702 of the mouse Snca gene on chromosome 6. The genomic sequences are from human assembly GRCh38.p14 and the mouse assembly GRCm39. The construct included a loxP-flanked neomycin selection cassette. In addition, there is also a SNCA non-coding antisense RNA in the human genome segment. The insertion disrupts Snca transcription. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6N-PRX-B6N embryonic stem cells (ES). The neomycin cassette was removed by transient expression of Cre. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts. The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J mice for at least 5 generations (see SNP note below) prior to sending males to The Jackson Laboratory Repository in 2024. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2024, a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (~9000 SNP) analysis was performed on the 2 males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. These data support a C57BL/6 genetic background predominantly comprised of C57BL/6J. The existence of the human genomic sequences may contribute to inability of data interpretation to predict percentages. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J allele-type with the exception of one marker (Chr.8 ~58 Mb) being heterozygous for C57BL/6J;C57BL/6N allele-type. Taken together, this suggests the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were predominantly C57BL/6J with some remaining contributions from C57BL/6N. In addition, there is also a SNCA non-coding antisense RNA in the human genome segment. The insertion disrupts Snca transcription. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6N-PRX-B6N embryonic stem cells (ES). The neomycin cassette was removed by transient expression of Cre. The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J mice for at least 5 generations (see SNP note below) prior to sending males to The Jackson Laboratory Repository in 2024. The existence of the human genomic sequences may contribute to inability of data interpretation to predict percentages. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J allele-type with the exception of one marker (Chr.8 ~58 Mb) being heterozygous for C57BL/6J;C57BL/6N allele-type. Browse References > Detailed Description α-Synuclein is a neuronal protein (coded by Snca) which plays a role in synaptic plasticity and neurotransmitter release. Mutations of Snca have been implicated in a group of neurodegenerative diseases that result from an accumulation of α-synuclein in neurons or, in some cases, glial cells. These disorders include Parkinson's disease (PDD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), the Lewy body variant of Alzheimer's disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation. These humanized A53T SNCA-GR (gene replacement) knock-in/knock-out mice carry a 158 kb fragment of human SNCA replacing the mouse Snca locus and the pathogenic A53T mutation (alanine to threonine) associated with early -onset Parkinson's disease. Mice homozygous for the mutation are viable and fertile with no obvious phenotype. These mice may be useful for studying SNCA function. Of note, the SNCA-GR model set also includes: B6J.B6N-Sncatm1.1(SNCA)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039166) and B6J.B6N-Sncatm3.1(SNCA*E46K)Mdk/J (Stock No. 039168). Read More Development The A53T SNCA-GR targeting vector was designed to insert a 158 kb (Chr4:89,707,185-89,865,027) fragment of the human SNCA (synuclein, alpha) carrying the A53T (alanine to threonine) mutation in place of Chr6:60,683,985-60,848,702 of the mouse Snca gene on chromosome 6. The genomic sequences are from human assembly GRCh38.p14 and the mouse assembly GRCm39. The construct included a loxP-flanked neomycin selection cassette. In addition, there is also a SNCA non-coding antisense RNA in the human genome segment. The insertion disrupts Snca transcription. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6N-PRX-B6N embryonic stem cells (ES). The neomycin cassette was removed by transient expression of Cre. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into blastocysts. The donating investigator reported that the resultant mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6J mice for at least 5 generations (see SNP note below) prior to sending males to The Jackson Laboratory Repository in 2024. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6J oocytes (Stock No. 000664). In 2024, a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (~9000 SNP) analysis was performed on the 2 males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. These data support a C57BL/6 genetic background predominantly comprised of C57BL/6J. The existence of the human genomic sequences may contribute to inability of data interpretation to predict percentages. Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). This showed all 48 markers to be C57BL/6J allele-type with the exception of one marker (Chr.8 ~58 Mb) being heterozygous for C57BL/6J;C57BL/6N allele-type. Taken together, this suggests the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were predominantly C57BL/6J with some remaining contributions from C57BL/6N.
